title: Managing Microscopy Data: Strategies and Challenges from a Core Perspective
content: Biological microscopy has come a long way in the past decade. From what was then the state-of-the-art, time-lapse fluorescence microscopy, to the current cutting-edge techniques of 3D light sheet imaging and spatial biology, these techniques provide more detailed observations of biological systems. Correspondingly, imaging datasets have grown in size. Likewise, image and data analysis techniques have also grown more sophisticated, both in the number of available tools, to the complexity of the analyses. However, the question remains: How do we best handle data to adhere to the Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR) guidelines?
